sources.title: Mahābhārata, Book 3 (Āraṇyakaparvan), Skanda’s birth and campaign, BORI Critical Edition, adhyāyas 213–221
sources.edition: Electronic text of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute Critical Edition; Unicode Roman (ISO 15919), based on Tokunaga’s version with John D. Smith revisions and BORI checking; edition statement and format documented at https://bombay.indology.info/mahabharata/statement.html and https://bombay.indology.info/mahabharata/welcome.html.
sources.locator: BORI CE 3.213–3.221; locators in claims are book.chapter.verse.

notes: Passage-limited extraction from the BORI Critical Edition of Mahābhārata Book 3, chapters 213–221: Devasenā’s encounter with Keśin, Skanda’s birth and divine reception, the named mother/attendant figures, the procession of Śiva, and Skanda’s battle with Mahīṣa.

The CE chapters contain fewer than 100 defensible individually named persons; this is not a 100-person roster. The batch records 39 newly source-scoped named people plus 13 existing graph anchors and three non-person class references, with explicit source-based relation or action claims. Group names, anonymous wives/warriors, stars, places, weapons, and generic gaṇas are excluded.

Clear graph anchors reused: Skanda, Indra, Śiva/Rudra, Agni, Varuṇa, Arundhatī, Kubera, Yama, Vāyu, Parjanya, Soma, Brahmā and Dakṣa. Viśākha remains source-scoped because its identity with similar graph names was not established in this passage.

Names with an explicit within-passage equation are represented once (Aditi/Revatī, Diti/Mukhamāṇḍikā, Dhātrī/Lohitāyanī; Skanda/Guha/Mahāsena/Kumāra/Kārttikeya; Śiva/Rudra/Hara). Female Rudrā and Mitrā from the seven mothers are not merged with male Rudra/Śiva or Mitra. The two occurrences of Āryā are kept separate because no explicit identity equation appears.

Vinatā’s statement that Skanda is her son is recorded as her claim in the source, not as a harmonized birth account. The text’s multiple birth explanations are represented as such; no single biological parentage is imposed.

Citra and Airāvata at 3.214.22–24 are explicitly called nāgas in this passage and are kept source-scoped, separate from the elephant Airāvata. Gāndhārī, Keśinī, Sāvitrī, Gaurī, and Vidyā in 3.221 are source-local figures; no identity with similarly named epic women is asserted.

The named twins Miñjikā and Miñjika are omitted as a pair because the passage does not individuate their referents. Rudra’s weapon Vijaya and animal/vehicle names are also omitted. Cattle, dogs, and nāgas appear only as non-person class reference nodes for explicit motherhood claims.
